about.title: Turlock Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone is not a legal problem first. It is an empty chair, a quiet kitchen, a routine that no longer makes sense. Still, when a death in Turlock happens because another person or business was careless, California law gives certain family members a way to hold them accountable in civil court. Public records show 331 injury collisions here in 2025, with 473 people hurt and one life lost, much of it along Lander Avenue, W Main Street, Geer Road and N Golden State Boulevard, and often in the Friday commute between 5 and 7 p.m. Behind that single fatality is a Stanislaus County household trying to figure out what comes next. Wrongful death claims are not limited to traffic, either; they can arise from farm and warehouse incidents, unsafe property, or medical errors. LawProactive does not practice law. We connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, meaning no fee is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Turlock Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who in your family is eligible before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: The general window is two years from the date of death, but it shrinks considerably when a government entity such as a city, county, or state agency is involved. Getting connected quickly protects that timeline.

items.title: Every category of loss accounted for
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Independent counsel works on contingency to pursue all of them.

items.question: My brother was killed in a crash on Geer Road and the other driver was charged. Do we have to wait for the criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs separately from any criminal prosecution in Stanislaus County. The two-year deadline keeps counting regardless of what happens in criminal court, so it is worth speaking with an attorney now. Evidence from the police investigation can often be useful in the civil case as well.

items.question: I am the adult child of the person who died. Can I file in California?
items.answer: Children, along with a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner, are first in line under California's wrongful death law. If there is no spouse, partner, or child, certain financially dependent relatives and heirs may qualify. An attorney can confirm where you and other family members stand.

items.question: What can a Turlock family actually recover?
items.answer: California allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. What that looks like depends entirely on your family's circumstances, and no one can promise a particular result. An independent attorney can walk through the specifics with you at no cost.
